environment_note: Reference run used CPython stdlib only. CI reruns the same deterministic campaign on ubuntu-latest.

tiny-plunge-1um.finding: 0.5 mm occupancy completely misses a real 0.001 mm plunge.

tiny-cusp-1um.finding: 0.5 mm occupancy erases the entire positive-volume 0.001 mm cusp and changes body existence.

cut-through-two-bodies.finding: Both bounded candidates preserve the obvious through-cut separation at this grid alignment.

high-segment-equivalent-100000.finding: Exact duplicate envelope canonicalization makes representation work depend on unique material boundaries rather than journal segmentation, while the journal event count remains explicit.

interpretation: The exact orthogonal cell/deferred-CSG prototype is exact and deterministic for its deliberately narrow axis-aligned planar subset, including lower-dimensional contact and disconnected bodies.
The sparse voxel prototype is robust and deterministic for coarse material occupancy but has an explicit resolution floor; it cannot be authoritative for sub-cell manufacturing features.

Neither prototype alone replaces an analytic B-rep kernel: the cell prototype does not cover arbitrary curved geometry, while voxel state requires surface extraction and analytic recognition before STEP.

The strongest architecture candidate is hybrid: preserve analytic/process/provenance semantics globally; permit exact/deferred cell-like or volumetric fallback locally; reconcile only bounded fallback regions back to conventional B-rep under the STEP contract.
